citations.note: Hatori and Oi (2026), Theorem 5.2, Example 5.3 and Corollary 6.2; the exact source from which the two-sided criterion is derived.
Tabor (2003), classical Fischer–Muszély stability on groups/Banach spaces; does not provide the positive-cone two-sided order-isomorphism criterion.
Dong, Leung and Li (2024), positive-cone approximate-isometry stability; a different metric perturbation framework.
Hirota and Oppekepenguin (2026), exact Fischer–Muszély equations on positive cones of C*-algebras; not the inverse approximate-FM criterion.

evidence: The two-sided criterion is a valid consequence of applying Hatori–Oi's approximate-FM stability theorem to T and T^{-1}. If L and M are the respective bounded positive linear asymptotic cores, uniform approximation gives a bound on ||ML(na)-na|| independent of n; linearity then forces ML=I after division by n, and the symmetric argument gives LM=I. The converse bounded-perturbation estimates are immediate three-error inequalities. The weighted c0 model is also correct: the scalar inverse is piecewise linear with slopes 1/(1+w) and 1/w, its superadditivity defect ranges from 0 to ε/w and is attained at the breakpoint, so Δ(T_w^{-1})=sup_n ε/w_n, with the stated phase transition.

independent_checks: Read Hatori–Oi Theorem 5.2 in open-access arXiv HTML: surjective approximate FM maps have a unique bounded positive linear core at finite uniform distance, with bound 3ε and dense positive image.
Read Hatori–Oi Example 5.3: T(x)_n=x_n/n+min{x_n,ε} is a continuous bijection with Δ(T)=ε whose linear core x_n/n is dense but not onto.
Re-derived ||ML(na)-na||≤3||M||ε+3δ and divided by n to force ML=I on A_+, then symmetrically LM=I.
For φ_w(t)=wt+min(t,ε), inverted the scalar map and checked d_w(u,v)=ψ_w(u+v)-ψ_w(u)-ψ_w(v) satisfies 0≤d_w≤ε/w, attaining ε/w at u=v=(1+w)ε.
Checked the c0 inverse is well-defined even when inf w_n=0: every null output is eventually in the first branch y/(1+w_n), so its inverse is again null.
limitations: The inherited factor 3 is not claimed sharp, and finite inverse FM defect is not claimed to be the weakest possible extra condition.
The exact ε/m inverse-defect formula is specific to the displayed diagonal c0 family.
A 2026 unpublished Hatori–Oi manuscript on order isomorphisms of non-unital C*-algebras is cited by the source but was not publicly accessible and was not claimed to have been read.

evidence: Hatori and Oi's source theorem supplies the unique positive linear approximation within 3ε and explicitly exhibits the w_n=1/n example where the core is dense but not surjective; its Corollary 6.2 gives a different sufficient lower-distance condition for an order-isomorphic core. The source does not state the inverse-FM if-and-only-if criterion, mutual-inverse core identity, or the arbitrary-weight exact inverse-defect formula. Targeted searches for two-sided/inverse Fischer–Muszély conditions and order-isomorphic asymptotic cores found no equivalent prior statement. The unpublished Hatori–Oi manuscript cited by the source was not accessible and remains a residual literature risk.

Although the main equivalence is a short argument once Hatori–Oi's theorem is available, it identifies an exact missing hypothesis for their non-surjective-core phenomenon and packages it with a quantitative c0 phase transition. This gives a useful structural test rather than merely another sufficient coarse lower bound.
